firstAttempt.summary: The same two cases were opened on 2026-10-05 with the first-attempt adapters (tasks 9 and 10). Finalize was not run before the kernel's judgment window closed. CloseFirstAttempt (2026-10-09) finalized both issues as the registry had already determined them and settled the kernel side.

outcome.A: Final x Decided(Yes) at finalize; adapter execute at 1791522804 (about 31 h after the judgment window closed) -> acceptFulfillment accepted and paid: the kernel bounds acceptFulfillment by settleBy only and settleBy = 0; Enacted; submission 9/1 Accepted
outcome.A2: Final x NoDecision (round 2 closed without ballots, REQUIRE_FRESH_DECISION); claimUnjudged(10, 1) paid the worker by the kernel default; submission 10/1 Accepted

firstAttempt.lesson: the adapter's own deadline (judgment window minus margin, decision #36) is the conservative bound it uses at open; whether a late acceptance is still legal is the kernel's call at execute, recorded as Enacted or Failed. Here the kernel accepted. A missed Finalize is therefore a bookkeeping gap, not a loss of funds in either direction, and the kernel default covers the NoDecision case.

gas.observed: Sepolia repriced between the two attempts: on 2026-10-05 base fee about 1.2 gwei, block gas limit 60M, adapter CREATE 1,335,381 gas, open 644,005 gas, mintTask 657,970 gas; on 2026-10-09 base fee 15-18 wei, block gas limit 200M, adapter CREATE 9,301,889 gas, open 2,740,485 gas, mintTask 3,752,448 gas. The local EVM model of the Foundry build under-estimates these costs five- to seven-fold, so transactions sized by the local simulation ran out of gas while the simulation passed.
gas.remedy: every broadcast after the first incident used --skip-simulation --gas-estimate-multiplier 150 (node-side eth_estimateGas); documented in docs/sepolia-runbook.md
